rgb: This is an open dirt or gravel dog park enclosed by fencing, with bare trees bordering the background approximately 20 to 30 metres ahead and left. During the first two frames, three dogs are positioned about 6 to 15 metres in front of the camera wearer: a black-and-tan dog at centre-right, a white dog slightly farther back and to its left, and a black-and-white dog farther left. Several people stand by the perimeter fence 15 to 25 metres away, facing into the enclosure. In frames 2 and 4, a person wearing a red hat is partly visible at the extreme left edge, within 1 metre of the camera wearer and mostly cropped out by the field of view. From frames 1 through 3, the camera angles downward toward the ground while the black-and-tan dog runs straight at the camera wearer, reducing its distance from roughly 10 metres to around 1.5 metres before disappearing below the bottom edge. At the same time, the white dog advances from about 12 metres away in the upper-left of frame 3 to approximately 3 metres directly ahead in frame 4, facing and watching the camera wearer; the black-and-white dog stays about 8 metres behind it on the left. By frame 5, the camera points steeply at the ground, with the white dog in the lower-left at a distance of 1 to 1.5 metres, just coming into arm's reach beside the camera wearer's extended left arm and a yellow leash along the bottom edge. The faraway fence and people have moved entirely out of view above the frame.
depth: The depth map depicts a broad, level ground surface with a smooth gradient from the bright foreground within 1 metre to the dark fence and trees around the perimeter, roughly 15 to 30 metres distant. In frames 1 and 2, three dogs occupy the central midground about 4 to 10 metres away and sit 1 to 3 metres apart. Farther back, people standing near the left and centre portions of the fence, approximately 15 to 25 metres away, appear with the dogs as small, brighter silhouettes rising above the ground gradient. A nearby person also enters partway at the far-left border within 1 metre in frame 2. As the camera angles downward in frame 3, a dark-and-tan dog advances directly ahead to about 1.5 to 2 metres away and below eye level, facing forward/right toward the route of the camera wearer. Two other dogs stay 8 to 10 metres behind in the upper-left, and another dog is partially outside the view at the far right. Across frames 4 and 5, a white dog moves closer on the left, progressing from about 3 metres ahead to roughly 1 to 1.5 metres away and nearly entering arm's reach beside either the camera wearer's dark sleeve/hand or an adjacent companion in the bottom-left corner, under 0.8 metres away and partly hidden by the frame edge. Compared with RGB alone, this map makes the uninterrupted ground-distance gradient visible and distinguishes the dark dogs and bottom-left foreground figure from the similarly dark mulch much more clearly. However, it is unreliable in frame 4, when the overall brightness falls abruptly as the ground tilts, and in frame 5, when the fast-moving white dog's outline blends into the ground.
segmentation: Against the unlabelled black background of the fenced dog park, the segmentation map separates individual foreground and midground subjects and follows their left-to-right changes throughout the five-frame sequence. In frames 1 and 2, it identifies one distant person by the centre fence, about 20 metres away and oriented roughly toward the field, plus two people on the left at distances of 15 to 20 metres. It also marks midground dogs 5 to 10 metres away and separated by several metres, but incorrectly labels them as 'sheep' and 'cow'. Nothing lies within the camera wearer's arm's reach except a person partially shown at the extreme left edge in frames 2 and 4, within 1 metre and heavily obscured by the left image boundary. In frame 3, a large green 'dog' mask covers the approaching dark-and-tan dog 1.5 to 2 metres ahead of and below the camera wearer, while a small brown 'person' mask identifies a distant figure 12 to 15 metres behind it in the upper-left. As the camera tips farther downward and rotates slightly right in frames 4 and 5, a yellow mask follows the white dog from roughly 3 metres away in the centre-left to 1 to 1.5 metres away on the left, nearly entering arm's reach of the unlabelled arm or sleeve at bottom-left, though the dog is incorrectly classified as a 'bird'. The masks make tiny distant figures among the busy trees and fence easier to locate than in RGB, but their semantic labels are highly unreliable, assigning 'sheep', 'cow', and 'bird' to dogs and 'person' to a background dog in frame 3. The map also entirely fails to detect several dogs and background bystanders that remain visible across the frames.
pose: Across all five frames, the pose map remains almost completely black and detects no human skeletons for either the bystanders 15 to 25 metres away or the partly visible person and arm along the bottom-left edge within 1 metre of the camera wearer. The sole result occurs in frame 3, where the system mistakenly places a small yellow body skeleton on the dark-and-tan dog positioned 1.5 to 2 metres in front of and below the camera wearer. This false pose follows the dog's torso and lowered head, which are angled toward the bottom-right, with inferred head and upper-body joints located around its snout and shoulders. No magenta hand keypoints are present anywhere in the strip. As a result, the pose map supplies no useful evidence about the facing directions of real people, whether they are looking at the camera wearer, or what falls within any person's arm's reach during the sequence. It adds no spatial information beyond the RGB imagery and is wholly unreliable in this case because it both falsely fits a human pose to a four-legged animal and fails to detect every actual human in the scene.
